title: San Francisco City Hall Hosts Its First Diwali Celebration With Mayor Lurie
excerpt: Organised by Indiaspora, the November 4 celebration brought Consul General Satish Sivan, Mayor Daniel Lurie and community leaders together for a ceremonial lamp lighting days before Diwali on November 8.
body:
• San Francisco City Hall hosted a Diwali celebration on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, described by the consulate as the hall's first, organised by Indiaspora.
  • India's Consul General in San Francisco, Satish Sivan, Mayor Daniel Lurie and Indiaspora founder MR Rangaswami attended, alongside city officials and community leaders.
  • The programme featured a ceremonial lamp lighting and traditional dance performances, according to the consulate's account and news coverage.
  • The celebration came days before the main Diwali day on Sunday, November 8, 2026.

San Francisco City Hall hosted a Diwali celebration on Wednesday, November 4, 2026 — billed by the organisers and the consulate as the hall's first — bringing together Indian and American dignitaries, city officials and community leaders to mark the Festival of Lights. The event was organised by Indiaspora, according to ANI reporting of the celebration.

Plan Your Visit

  • Date: Wednesday, November 4, 2026
  • Venue: San Francisco City Hall
  • Admission: Not stated in the announcement coverage — see the Consulate General of India in San Francisco post for the official account of the event.
  • Official page: Consulate General of India, San Francisco

What Happened at City Hall

India's Consul General in San Francisco, Satish Sivan, and San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie attended the celebration, and Indiaspora founder MR Rangaswami was also present. The Consulate General of India in San Francisco shared details of the event in a social media post, describing it as a historic occasion that brought Diwali traditions to the heart of the city.

"A historic Diwali celebration at San Francisco City Hall!" the post read, according to ANI. The celebration featured a ceremonial lamp-lighting ceremony. Photographs shared alongside the post showed dignitaries at the podium with Indian and American flags, group portraits on City Hall's grand staircase and traditional dance performances before a large gathering, ANI reported. Inshorts, summarising the same celebration, also noted the lamp lighting and traditional dance performances.

Why the Setting Matters

According to the consulate, the event highlighted the enduring cultural ties between India and the United States, as well as the contributions of the Indian-American community to San Francisco. The post further described the gathering as "a landmark occasion bringing the spirit and traditions of Diwali to the heart of the city."

For Bay Area readers, the significance is the venue itself. A Diwali programme inside City Hall, attended by the mayor and India's consul general, places a festival long celebrated in homes, temples and community halls in the city's civic centre. That is the development the organisers and the consulate emphasised in their account of the evening.

Days Before the Main Festival

The City Hall celebration came ahead of the main Diwali festival day, which falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026. ANI noted that the date is determined by the Amavasya Tithi, or new moon night, in the Hindu lunar month of Kartik, and that this year's festival falls later than its usual October window following an additional lunar month, known as Adhik Maas, earlier in the year.

The five-day festival begins with Dhanteras on November 6, followed by Choti Diwali on November 7. Diwali and Lakshmi Puja are celebrated on November 8, followed by Govardhan Puja on November 9 and Bhai Dooj on November 10, according to ANI.

What to Watch Next

The reports of the City Hall event do not state whether it will become an annual fixture, and no details of a future edition were given in the coverage. Readers who want the official record of this year's celebration can see the photographs and description in the consulate's post. For families in San Francisco, the immediate next step is the festival itself this weekend, culminating in Diwali on Sunday, November 8.
